name: RJ45 Ethernet Connector
short_description: The standard 8P8C modular connector used to connect devices to Ethernet local area networks.
common_uses: Network routers, IP cameras, PC ethernet ports, industrial Modbus TCP connections.

quick_facts.passive_active: Passive (without magnetics) / Active (with built-in MagJack transformers)
quick_facts.typical_current: 350mA (standard) / up to 1A for Power over Ethernet (PoE)

specifications.notes: Isolates signal lines and reduces EMI noise

definition: An RJ45 (Registered Jack 45) connector is an 8-position, 8-contact (8P8C) modular connector standard. It is the universal interface used for twisted-pair Ethernet cabling, connecting computers, routers, and switches to local area networks (LAN).
working_principle: It routes differential transmit and receive data signals (TX/RX) over twisted-pair copper cables. High-speed digital signals are passed through internal isolation transformers (magnetics) to suppress common-mode noise and prevent ground loop currents.
types: Standard RJ45 jacks, MagJacks (with integrated transformers), and shielded metal RJ45 connectors.
construction: Houses 8 gold-plated spring wire contacts inside a clear polycarbonate plug casing, mating with a shielded copper-alloy PCB jack housing.
electrical_characteristics: Low contact resistance, matched 100Ω differential impedance, and high dielectric isolation. Supports Power over Ethernet (PoE).
symbol_description: An 8-pin block showing TX/RX differential pairs, ground shielding, and LED connections.
formulas: Ethernet line differential impedance: Z_diff = 100 Ω.
applications: Network switches, desktop computers, IP network cameras, and smart home hubs.
advantages: Universal global standard, supports high-speed data (up to 10 Gbps), supports Power over Ethernet (PoE).
disadvantages: Bulky physical size, requires differential trace routing and isolation transformers, plastic locking clip on plugs breaks easily.
example_circuit_operation: An RJ45 MagJack is soldered to a microchip board. The signal pins route through the integrated isolation magnetics to an Ethernet PHY chip, allowing the board to communicate over a local router network.
practical_tips: When designing a PCB with an RJ45 port, select a 'MagJack' (an RJ45 connector with integrated magnetics). This saves significant board space and simplifies routing by enclosing the transformers and filter chokes inside the connector shell.

interview_questions.question: What does 8P8C stand for?
interview_questions.answer: 8 Positions, 8 Contacts, describing the physical connector configuration of an RJ45 plug or jack.

interview_questions.question: What is a MagJack and why is it used?
interview_questions.answer: An RJ45 jack with integrated isolation transformers and common-mode chokes. It isolates the transceiver chip from high line voltages, suppresses EMI, and saves board space.

interview_questions.question: How do the T568A and T568B wiring standards differ?
interview_questions.answer: They differ in the color arrangement of the orange and green twisted wire pairs. T568B is the dominant standard used in modern network patch cables.

interview_questions.question: What is Power over Ethernet (PoE)?
interview_questions.answer: A technology that allows DC power to be transmitted along with data over standard Ethernet cables, powering IP cameras or VoIP phones without separate power cords.

interview_questions.question: Why are ethernet signals routed as differential pairs?
interview_questions.answer: Differential routing cancels out electromagnetic noise. Noise coupled onto the twisted cable affects both wires equally and is rejected by the receiver's differential amplifier.

references: IEEE 802.3 Ethernet Standards; Amphenol RJ45 design specs.
